solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Around noon, day before, say Black Prince danced with her (10)

indicators.note: CILLA goes around the letters for noon, day and before

blocks.note: Cilla Black, the Liverpool singer and TV presenter; 'say' flags her as one example of a Black

annotation.surface: A garbled timeline of an afternoon at court, with a Black Prince doing the dancing.
annotation.walkthrough: The Black Prince is a real historical figure, so 'Black' seems tied to 'Prince'; it belongs with 'say' instead. Cilla Black was a hugely famous British singer and presenter of the TV show Blind Date.
annotation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the prince dances with Cinderella at the ball.

clue.text: Hostile island to the north of California supports mini uprising (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the island sits above California
in a down clue, what supports another piece sits under it
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

blocks.note: Cal is the short form of California

annotation.surface: A hostile island off the Californian coast backs a small rebellion.
annotation.walkthrough: The down-clue grammar does all the work: I over CAL makes the bottom half, and that half holds up the upturned MINI.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Latin-rooted word for unfriendly, from inimicus, enemy.

clue.text: Finish off drug propping up party animal (3)

indicators.note: the finish of 'drug' is its last letter
in a down clue, G sits under DO and holds it up

annotation.surface: A party animal finishing off the drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party animal' reads as a phrase, but the break comes between them: 'party' is DO and 'animal' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the most familiar household pet stands for animal in general.

clue.text: Two different rivers associated with country (5)

blocks.note: R = river, the first of the two
the Ural, the river dividing Europe from Asia

annotation.surface: A geography note: two rivers linked with one nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a noun meaning nation; here it is the adjective, as in country life.
annotation.definitionFit: Rural and country both describe life outside towns.

clue.text: One potted starter of lemon sorbet ordered (7)

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter
the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: A restaurant order: something potted, then a lemon sorbet.
annotation.walkthrough: Menu words disguise it: 'starter' and 'ordered' feel like dining, but one takes a first letter and the other stirs the letters. Lobsters are caught in lobster pots.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: this shellfish is trapped in pots, and is also served potted, so 'one potted' fits either way.

clue.text: Valiant maiden shortly embraces warrior king (9)

indicators.note: ANON wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: M = maiden, a scoreless over in cricket

annotation.surface: A brave young woman briefly hugs a warrior king.
annotation.walkthrough: The container word comes last, so read it as 'shortly embraces valiant maiden'. Agamemnon led the Greeks at Troy.
annotation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the Greek king who led the army at Troy.

clue.text: Obscure British band (4)

blocks.note: to make hazy, hard to see
the Britpop group fronted by Damon Albarn

annotation.surface: A little-known group from Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the band; it is a verb, and the band is famous, anything but obscure.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym (to smudge from view) paired with a proper name: the 1990s Britpop band.

clue.text: Place bro had renovated? (8,3)

indicators.note: a renovated place is rebuilt, so the letters are rebuilt

annotation.surface: Wondering whether the flat a brother owned has been done up.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of PLACE BRO HAD rebuild into the answer, and the whole reads as a description of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A bachelor pad is the sort of home a single young bloke keeps.

clue.text: Expose US Navy periodically spinning untruth (6)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals
something spinning turns about, so the word faces the other way

annotation.surface: Exposing the US Navy for repeatedly spinning a false story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' reads as political spin, but it just turns LIE round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: taking the cover off something lays it open to view.

clue.text: Family snatch cold cuts and seafood (4,4)

indicators.note: to cut something is to slice into it, so C goes into the middle of GRAB

annotation.surface: A family grabbing cold cuts and seafood from a buffet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold cuts' is a deli phrase for sliced meat, but here 'cold' is C and 'cuts' tells it to split GRAB.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this giant long-legged crustacean is a prized item on seafood menus.

clue.text: Onset of ardent romance when touring Cape Bay (6)

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter
LOVE goes round C, as a tourist goes round a place

annotation.surface: A holiday fling starting on a tour of a cape and its bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bay' is not the sea here; it is a recess in a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its architectural sense: a bay is a recess set back into a wall.

clue.text: Relief is calculated, in part, based on tax revenues? (6)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words before it

annotation.surface: A tax guide explaining that relief is partly worked out from revenue.
annotation.walkthrough: The tax-return wording makes the whole clue look like the definition; only the last words are.
annotation.definitionFit: Fiscal describes anything to do with government revenue and taxation.

clue.text: Where to keep good clarets fresh? (4,7)

definitions.text: Where to keep good clarets fresh?

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters come out in a new form

annotation.surface: A wine lover asking where best to store fine claret.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
annotation.definitionFit: Cold storage keeps things fresh, as a cool cellar does for wine.

clue.text: The US band with popular electronic instrument (8)

annotation.surface: An American band featuring a well-liked electronic instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like filler but is part of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The theremin is an early electronic instrument played without touch.

clue.text: Injure supporter in capital relocating northern star (6,6)

indicators.note: the supporter is placed inside the capital, splitting LONDON after LON
to relocate is to move house, so one N of LONDON moves to a new spot

blocks.note: the start of LONDON, the UK capital
a bra is a supporting garment
N = northern: LONDON's final N, moved here from the end
the rest of LONDON, now without its last N

annotation.surface: A northern celebrity moving to the capital gets hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Northern' looks like a description of the star; it is N, one of the two in LONDON, which shifts one place.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the actor of The Godfather and On the Waterfront is one Hollywood star.

clue.text: Very old one stupidly drunk on this in ancient Rome (9)

indicators.note: the letters of ONE are arranged foolishly

annotation.surface: An old Roman getting foolishly drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: HIC also sounds like a drunkard's hiccup, which the surface plays on.
annotation.definitionFit: Neolithic refers to the late Stone Age, so very old.

clue.text: An international compiler failing to finish drink (8)

indicators.note: SETTER does not get to its last letter

annotation.surface: A global crossword setter who can't finish a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The compiler is the setter of the crossword.
annotation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Quiet old Conservative Big Beast last to speak in vibrant tone (8,4)

indicators.note: the last letter of 'speak'

blocks.note: a Big Beast in politics is a heavyweight, a kingpin

annotation.surface: A veteran Tory heavyweight keeps quiet until last, then speaks in a vivid tone.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'big beast' is a senior, powerful figure, which is why it gives KINGPIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Shocking pink is a vivid, intense shade of pink.

clue.text: US writer, dear, popular, regularly wears silk (7)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken and the rest skipped
KC wears the letters, so goes round them

blocks.note: a silk is a King's Counsel, a senior barrister, KC

annotation.surface: An American author, beloved and popular, often dresses in silk.
annotation.walkthrough: A senior British barrister is called a silk after the silk gown they wear, abbreviated KC.
annotation.definitionFit: Jack Kerouac was the American author of On the Road.

clue.text: Bill eats fruit out of English tree (6)

indicators.note: AD takes the fruit inside it
fruit 'out of English' is fruit with its English taken away, so E leaves LEMON

blocks.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a bill posted up

annotation.surface: Bill eats fruit from an English tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name; it is AD, a poster.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the word names both the nut and the blossoming tree that bears it.

clue.text: More depressed, with nasty grime covering lavatory (8)

indicators.note: the letters of GRIME are rearranged
the rearranged GRIME goes over LOO

annotation.surface: Someone feels worse on finding a grimy toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British for toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, matching comparative for comparative: sadder, lower in spirits.

clue.text: Decent return FTSE domestics reduced (6)

indicators.note: read the letters backwards
only part of the words is used

blocks.note: ftSE DOMestics, read right to left

annotation.surface: A modest return on FTSE domestic shares, marked down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like an investment return, but it tells you to read backwards. The FTSE is the London stock market index.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of proper and seemly, as said of dress or behaviour.

clue.text: Duplicate chapter covered by US school subject (5)

indicators.note: MATH covers C, so it sits inside

blocks.note: the American short form of mathematics

annotation.surface: A chapter copied out of an American maths textbook.
annotation.walkthrough: Americans say math, Britons maths, hence 'US'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to equal or copy something exactly, as in matching a rival's offer.

clue.text: I’m obliged to enter swanky compound (6)

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the thanks goes inside the swanky word

annotation.surface: Someone grateful to be let into a smart walled estate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like an enclosure; it is a chemical compound.
annotation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound used in fertiliser.

clue.text: Last lieutenant stationed in United India and China (8)

indicators.note: LT is placed inside U I MATE

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names
I = India in the phonetic alphabet
china = mate, from rhyming slang china plate

annotation.surface: An officer's final posting to a united India and China.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: final, coming at the very end of a series.

clue.text: Mum! New fella? (3)

annotation.surface: A child asking their mother about her new boyfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum!' reads as a cry to the mother, but it just gives MA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fella is informal for a male, and in the surface also means a boyfriend.

clue.text: Boundary stroke by batsman (4)

blocks.note: in cricket, a shot that glances off the side of the bat

annotation.surface: A cricket shot sent to the boundary.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket 'boundary' is a four or six, so the surface is all cricket; but the first meaning is just a border. An edge is a shot off the side of the bat.
annotation.definitionFit: An edge is a boundary, and in cricket an edge is a shot off the bat's edge.

clue.text: Clumsy article penned by dad — check working (4-6)

indicators.note: a thing penned is shut in a pen, an enclosure, so the article is shut inside DAD
the letters are set to work, so rearranged

blocks.note: as printed; AN goes inside it, making DANAD

annotation.surface: A clumsy writer's article, written by Dad, needs checking.
annotation.walkthrough: Cack-handed is British informal for clumsy.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: British informal slang for awkward with the hands, originally meaning left-handed.
